subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finpay.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@finpay.com>
Date: 2027-06-26T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up

Hi Laura / Raj,

Thanks for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

- Requirements / notes from call:
  - Target latency: p95 < 100ms for short generation flows (<=64 tokens)
  - Throughput: sustained 200-300 requests/sec for embeddings + bursts to 1k+ for spikes
  - Context length: mostly <= 8k, with some longer batch jobs
  - Data security: currently fine with hosted during pilot; production needs consideration for Dedicated or Private VPC

- Recommendation:
  - Pilot: Hosted API to iterate quickly and validate prompts/quality
  - Production: Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and lower p95 latency; Private only if you need VPC or on-prem isolation

Next steps:
1) We can run a 48-72h benchmark using a synthetic workload scoped to your token distribution (I can trigger this)
2) If you want predictable p95 latency at scale, we’ll size a Dedicated cluster (I’ll loop in Dylan for sizing)
3) I’ve attached a benchmark template and our Dedicated SLA for your review

Would you like us to schedule the benchmark for this week or next? If you prefer, we can start the Hosted pilot immediately and switch to Dedicated once results look good.

Best,

Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency/throughput decision follow-up

Hi Laura — great questions, thanks. Short answers and proposed concrete options below.

1) Expected p95 (short prompts, <=64 tokens):
   - Hosted API (Redwood managed): typical p95 in our benchmark fleet is ~100-140ms depending on model and region; for conservative planning assume ~120ms for your token distribution.
   - Dedicated capacity: with a properly sized pool and optimized batching (plus KV caching for repeated prefixes) we typically see p95 ~40-80ms for the same models; for your target I would size for mid-range ~60ms p95 as a conservative estimate.

2) Autoscale & burst: Dedicated supports reserved capacity with configurable burst policies. You can reserve baseline capacity for steady throughput and enable burst nodes (ephemeral) for traffic spikes — we also support automatic fallback to Hosted for additional headroom if configured.

Sizing suggestion for initial Dedicated pilot (based on your 200-300 qps sustained + expected bursts):
- Start: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared across the pool) with configuration to allow 2x burst nodes
- We'll tune batching and KV cache to minimize p95 for short flows

Options to proceed:
A) Hosted pilot (fast): 2-week pilot on Hosted to validate prompt quality and measure real-world token distribution. If results meet latency needs, we can keep Hosted; otherwise migrate to Dedicated.
B) Dedicated pilot (predictable): 2-4 week dedicated pilot with reserved nodes and a short SOW. We’ll run the benchmark workload and iterate on sizing.

I attached the benchmark template (latency_benchmark_results.csv) and our Dedicated SLA (redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf). I can schedule the benchmark run as early as Monday — would you prefer Monday or Wednesday for kickoff?

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm pilot type (Hosted vs Dedicated)
- If Dedicated: sign a short MSA/addendum and we’ll kick off sizing with Dylan
- If Hosted: I’ll provision pilot keys and benchmark credentials

Best,
